questions.question: Determine the slope of the line represented by the equation 4x + 6y = 12. ?
questions.questionHtml: Determine the slope of the line represented by the equation 4x + 6y = 12. ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any linear equation in the general form Ax + By = C, the slope (m) is given by the formula −A / B.

From the given equation 4x + 6y = 12, we identify A = 4 and B = 6.

Substituting these values: slope (m) = −4 / 6.

On simplifying the fraction by dividing by 2, we get −2 / 3.

∴ The correct answer is −2 / 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation of the line: 4x + 6y = 12

Formula Used:

Equation of a line in slope-intercept form: y = mx + c

For Ax + By + C = 0, Slope (m) = -A / B

Calculation:

Rewrite the equation in standard form:

⇒ 4x + 6y - 12 = 0

Compare with Ax + By + C = 0:

⇒ A = 4, B = 6

Substitute into the slope formula:

⇒ m = -A / B

⇒ m = -4 / 6

⇒ m = -2 / 3

∴ The slope of the line is -2 / 3.

Additional Information

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation y = mx + c defines a line with slope m and y-intercept c, which is where the line crosses the y-axis.

Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

Two lines are parallel if their slopes are equal (m1 = m2) and perpendicular if the product of their slopes is −1 (m1 × m2 = −1).

Types of Slopes

A positive slope means the line rises from left to right, while a negative slope means it falls. Horizontal lines have a slope of 0, and vertical lines have an undefined slope.

questions.question: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 120 degrees and a radius of 16 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of 2π / 3 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 120 degrees and a radius of 16 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of 2π/ 3 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert 2π/3 radians to degrees: (2/3) × 180° = 120°.

Since both sectors have the same radius (16 cm) and the same central angle (120°), their areas must be identical.

Identical areas always result in a ratio of 1 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1:1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = 16 cm

Central Angle 1 (θ1) = 120°

Central Angle 2 (θ2) = 2π/3 radians

Formula Used:

Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr2 (when θ is in degrees)

Area of sector = (1/2) × r2 × θ (when θ is in radians)

Calculations:

⇒ Convert θ2 to degrees: θ2 = (2π/3) × (180/π) = 120°

⇒ Area1 = (120/360) × π × (16)2 = (1/3) × 256π cm2

⇒ Area2 = (120/360) × π × (16)2 = (1/3) × 256π cm2

⇒ Ratio = Area1 : Area2 = [(1/3) × 256π] : [(1/3) × 256π]

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 1

∴ The correct answer is 1:1.

Additional Information

Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π. Conversely, multiply degrees by π/180 to get radians.

Arc Length of a Sector

The length of the arc (l) is given by l = r × θ, where θ must be in radians.

Relationship between Area and Arc Length

The area of a sector can also be calculated as Area = (1/2) × l × r, where l is the arc length and r is the radius.

questions.question: Based on geometric laws, a triangle can have:
questions.questionHtml: Based on geometric laws, a triangle can have:

options.text: One right angle and two acute angles
options.html: One right angle and two acute angles

options.text: Three acute angles each measuring more than 60°
options.html: Three acute angles each measuring more than 60°

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the Angle Sum Property, the sum of internal angles of a triangle is exactly 180°.

If a triangle has two right angles (90° + 90° = 180°), the third angle must be 0°, which is impossible.

If it has two obtuse angles (each > 90°), the sum will exceed 180°.

If all three acute angles are > 60°, the sum will exceed 180° (e.g., 61° × 3 = 183°).

A right-angled triangle must have one 90° angle and two acute angles that sum to 90°.

∴ The correct answer is One right angle and two acute angles.

Alternate Method

Given: Geometric laws of a triangle.

Formula Used: Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

Let the three interior angles of the triangle be ∠A, ∠B, and ∠C.

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ Let ∠C = 90° (Right angle)

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 180° − 90°

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 90°

⇒ Since every angle in a triangle must be greater than 0°, then ∠A < 90° and ∠B < 90°.

⇒ Angles less than 90° are classified as acute angles.

⇒ Thus, a triangle can consist of one right angle and two acute angles.

∴ The correct answer is One right angle and two acute angles.

Additional Information

Types of Triangles based on Angles

Acute Triangle: All three angles are less than 90°. Right Triangle: One angle is exactly 90°. Obtuse Triangle: One angle is greater than 90°.

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side: a + c, b + c > a, and a + c > b.

Exterior Angle Property

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two interior opposite angles.

questions.question: Line M serves as the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting point J(4, 10) and point K(16, -2). What is the y-intercept of line M?
questions.questionHtml: Line M serves as the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting point J(4, 10) and point K(16, -2). What is the y-intercept of line M?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find the midpoint of J(4, 10) and K(16, -2): (4+16)/2 = 10 and (10-2)/2 = 4. Midpoint is (10, 4).

Calculate slope of JK: (-2 − 10) / (16 − 4) = −12 / 12 = −1.

The perpendicular slope of line M is 1 (since −1 × 1 = −1).

Equation of line M: y − 4 = 1(x − 10) ⇒ y = x − 10 + 4 ⇒ y = x − 6.

The y-intercept occurs when x = 0, so y = −6.

∴ The correct answer is -6.

Alternate Method

Given:

Point J = (4, 10)

Point K = (16, −2)

Line M is the perpendicular bisector of JK.

Formula Used:

Midpoint = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2)

Slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁)

Slope of the perpendicular line = −1 ÷ (Slope)

Equation of a line: y = mx + c

Calculation:

⇒ Midpoint of JK

⇒ x = (4 + 16) ÷ 2 = 10

⇒ y = (10 + (−2)) ÷ 2 = 4

⇒ Midpoint = (10, 4)

⇒ Slope of JK

⇒ (−2 − 10) ÷ (16 − 4) = −12 ÷ 12 = −1

⇒ Slope of line M = 1 (negative reciprocal of −1)

⇒ Equation of line M passing through (10, 4)

⇒ y − 4 = 1(x − 10)

⇒ y = x − 6

⇒ y-intercept when x = 0

⇒ y = −6

∴ The y-intercept of line M is −6.

Additional Information

Perpendicular Slopes Property

If two lines are perpendicular, the product of their slopes is −1 (m1 × m2 = −1), provided neither line is vertical.

Equation of a Line (Slope-Intercept Form)

The equation y = mx + c represents a line where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept, which is the value of y when x = 0.

Midpoint Formula

The midpoint of a segment with endpoints (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by M = [(x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2].

questions.question: The area of triangle XYZ is 32 square cm. If a similar triangle PQR has sides that are four times the length of triangle XYZ's sides, what is the area of triangle PQR?
questions.questionHtml: The area of triangle XYZ is 32 square cm. If a similar triangle PQR has sides that are four times the length of triangle XYZ's sides, what is the area of triangle PQR?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Side Ratio (k) = 4

Area Ratio = k2 = 42 = 16

Area of ΔPQR = 16 × Area of ΔXYZ

Area of ΔPQR = 16 × 32 = 512 sq cm

∴ The correct answer is 512 sq cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of ▵XYZ = 32 cm2

Sides of ▵PQR are 4 times the corresponding sides of ▵XYZ

Formula Used:

Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (Ratio of corresponding sides)2

Calculation:

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = 4 : 1

⇒ Ratio of areas = (4)2 = 16

⇒ Area of ▵PQR = 16 × 32

⇒ Area of ▵PQR = 512 cm2

∴ The area of ▵PQR is 512 cm2.

Additional Information

Properties of Similar Triangles

For two similar triangles with side ratio k, the ratio of their corresponding perimeters, medians, and altitudes is also k.

Area-Side Relationship

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides: Area1/Area2 = (s1/s2)2.

Volume for 3D Shapes

For similar 3D figures, the ratio of their volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions: Vol1/Vol2 = k3.

Identify the algebraic identity: If a + b + c = 0, then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Here, a = 88, b = 70, and c = −158.

⇒ Substituting values: 3 × 88 × 70 × (−158)

⇒ 264 × 70 × (−158)

⇒ 18480 × (−158)

⇒ −2919840

∴ The correct answer is −2919840.

Algebraic Expansion

The general cubic expansion is a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca).

Conditional Identity

When the sum of three variables is zero, the sum of their cubes is exactly equal to three times their product (3abc).

Square of a Trinomial

The square of a trinomial is given by (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca).

questions.question: If sin A + cos A = 10 / 8, find the value of sin 2A. ?
questions.questionHtml: If sin A + cos A = 10 / 8, find the value of sin 2A. ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct identity: (sin A + cos A)2 = 1 + sin 2A.

Substitute the given value: (10 / 8)2 = 1 + sin 2A.

⇒ 100 / 64 = 1 + sin 2A.

⇒ sin 2A = (100 / 64) − 1 = 36 / 64 = 9 / 16.

∴ The correct answer is 9 / 16.

Alternate Method

Given: sin A + cos A = 10 / 8 = 5 / 4.

Formula Used: (sin A + cos A)2 = sin2 A + cos2 A + 2 sin A cos A; sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A.

⇒ sin A + cos A = 10 / 8

⇒ (sin A + cos A)2 = (10 / 8)2

⇒ sin2 A + cos2 A + 2 sin A cos A = 100 / 64

⇒ 1 + sin 2A = 25 / 16

⇒ sin 2A = (25 / 16) − 1

⇒ sin 2A = (25 − 16) / 16

⇒ sin 2A = 9 / 16

∴ The correct answer is 9 / 16.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

The fundamental identity is sin2 A + cos2 A = 1, which relates the squares of sine and cosine of the same angle.

Double Angle Formulas

sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A and cos 2A = cos2 A − sin2 A. These formulas are used to reduce or expand trigonometric expressions involving double angles.

Sum and Difference Relation

The relationship (sin A ± cos A)2 = 1 ± sin 2A is a very common shortcut for competitive exams to link the sum/difference of sine and cosine with the sine of the double angle.

questions.question: From an external point M, two tangents, MX and MY, are drawn to a circle. Given that the length of MX is 24 cm, what is the length of MY?
questions.questionHtml: From an external point M, two tangents, MX and MY, are drawn to a circle. Given that the length of MX is 24 cm, what is the length of MY?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the Theorem of Tangents, the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal.

⇒ Tangent MX = Tangent MY

⇒ Given MX = 24 cm, therefore MY = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

External point = M

Tangent 1 = MX = 24 cm

Tangent 2 = MY

Property Used:

For any circle, two tangents drawn from the same external point have congruent lengths.

Calculations:

⇒ In ▵MXO and ▵MYO:

⇒ OX = OY (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ OM = OM (Common side)

⇒ ∠MXO = ∠MYO = 90° (Tangent is perpendicular to the radius)

⇒ By RHS Congruence Criterion, ▵MXO ≅ ▵MYO.

⇒ By CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles):

⇒ MX = MY

⇒ Since MX = 24 cm, then MY = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (∠OXM = 90°).

External Point Tangent Angles

The center of the circle lies on the angle bisector of the angle between the two tangents (∠XMO = ∠YMO).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

Quadrilateral MXOY is a cyclic quadrilateral because the sum of opposite angles ∠X and ∠Y is 180° (90° + 90°).

questions.question: A circle is inscribed within a right triangle. Considering that the lengths of the two legs measure 12 cm and 16 cm, what is the radius of the inscribed circle?
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed within a right triangle. Considering that the lengths of the two legs measure 12 cm and 16 cm, what is the radius of the inscribed circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a right-angled triangle, the inradius r is given by: (Base + Height − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Given legs are 12 cm and 16 cm.

Hypotenuse = √(122 + 162) = 20 cm.

Inradius = (12 + 16 − 20) ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Leg 1 (a) = 12 cm

Leg 2 (b) = 16 cm

Formula Used:

Hypotenuse (c) = √(a2 + b2)

Inradius (r) = (a + b − c) ÷ 2

⇒ Hypotenuse (c) = √(122 + 162)

⇒ c = √(144 + 256) = √400 = 20 cm.

⇒ Inradius (r) = (12 + 16 − 20) ÷ 2

⇒ r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Additional Information

General Inradius Formula

For any triangle, the inradius (r) is equal to the Area (Δ) ÷ semi-perimeter (s).

Circumradius of a Right Triangle

The circumradius (R) is exactly half of the hypotenuse, and the circumcenter lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

Area and Perimeter Relation

The area of a right triangle is 1/2 × base × height, while the semi-perimeter (s) is (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

questions.question: If x = 0.04, y = 0.06, z = -0.10, and x + y + z = 0, find the value of (x 3 + y 3 + z 3 ) ÷ (3xyz) ?
questions.questionHtml: If x = 0.04, y = 0.06, z = -0.10, and x + y + z = 0, find the value of (x3 + y3 + z3) ÷ (3xyz)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If the sum of three variables x + y + z = 0, then the algebraic identity states that x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz.

Given: 0.04 + 0.06 + (−0.10) = 0.10 − 0.10 = 0.

Therefore, the numerator (x3 + y3 + z3) is exactly equal to the denominator 3xyz.

Result = 3xyz ÷ 3xyz = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: x = 0.04, y = 0.06, z = −0.10

Formula Used: x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 − xy − yz − zx)

⇒ Check the sum of variables: x + y + z = 0.04 + 0.06 + (−0.10)

⇒ x + y + z = 0.10 − 0.10 = 0

⇒ Substitute this into the formula: x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (0) × (x2 + y2 + z2 − xy − yz − zx)

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = 0

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz

⇒ Required value = (x3 + y3 + z3) ÷ (3xyz)

⇒ Value = 3xyz ÷ 3xyz = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

The Conditional Identity

The relation x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz is satisfied if x + y + z = 0 or if x = y = z.

Sum of Cubes Formula

For two variables, a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Square of a Trinomial

The expansion of (x + y + z)2 is x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx).

questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: ‘A person who actively supports reform or change’
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

‘A person who actively supports reform or change’
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Reformer.

Key Points

  • The word "Reformer" refers to a person who actively supports or advocates for reform or change, especially in social, political, or economic systems. (सुधारक)
    • Example: Mahatma Gandhi was a great reformer who worked for social and political change in India.
  • Reformers are often individuals who challenge the status quo and work towards progress and improvement, often in societal structures or policies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Reformer.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Traditionalist (परंपरावादी): A person who adheres to traditional views, customs, or practices and resists change.
    • Example: As a traditionalist, he prefers to celebrate festivals in the old-fashioned way.
  • Loyalist (अनुरक्त व्यक्ति): Someone who is loyal to a person, group, or government, especially in the face of opposition.
    • Example: The loyalist supported the monarchy during the political upheaval.
  • Conservative (रूढ़िवादी): A person who holds traditional values and is resistant to change or innovation.
    • Example: His conservative views on education often clash with modern approaches.

questions.question: Change the following from active to passive: They were screening the documentary at 9 pm.
questions.questionHtml:
Change the following from active to passive:

They were screening the documentary at 9 pm.

options.text: The documentary is screened at 9 pm.

options.html: The documentary had been screened at 9 pm.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "They were screening the documentary at 9 pm."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the documentary" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "were screening" to "was being screened" (past continuous passive).
  • The time phrase "at 9 pm" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The documentary was being screened at 9 pm."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The documentary is screened at 9 pm." – Incorrect tense (present simple passive).
  • Option 2: "The documentary had been screened at 9 pm." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
  • Option 4: "The documentary was screened at 9 pm." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).
